example.pinyin: Bùguǎn zěnyàng, wǒ dōu zhīchí nǐ.
example.english: No matter what, I support you.

note: Movement out and away from the speaker; 出來 chū lái is out toward the speaker. Also follows verbs: 走出去 zǒu chū qù (walk out).

example.english: What time are you coming home?

hint: the same (one), as in same day
note: Mostly in set forms: 同一個 tóng yī ge (the same one), 不同 bù tóng (different), 同學 tóng xué (classmate). Other reading tòng, only in 胡同 hú tòng (alley).

example.pinyin: Wǒmen shì tóng yī tiān shēngrì.

example.english: I've been watching my diet lately.

gloss: to do; to make; to mess with
note: A catch-all verb: 弄壞 nòng huài (to break), 弄好 nòng hǎo (to get it done), 弄丟 nòng diū (to lose). MOE's other reading is lòng (lane), as in 巷弄 xiàng lòng and addresses, but most Taiwanese say nòng when reading an address.

example.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ wǒ de shǒujī nònghuài le!

note: Formal or written; in everyday speech people say 媽媽 mā ma. 母親節 mǔ qīn jié = Mother's Day.
夠了 gòu le! (That's enough!) 不夠 bù gòu (not enough). Before an adjective it can mean really: 夠辣 gòu là (plenty spicy).

example.pinyin: Wǒmen de qián gòu bù gòu?

gloss: to pick up (a person); to answer
hint: meet a person; take a call
note: 接電話 jiē diàn huà (answer the phone), 接人 jiē rén (pick someone up), 接球 jiē qiú (catch a ball).

example.english: I'll pick you up after work.

note: Taiwan (MOE) says rèn wù with a full tone; mainland often rèn wu.

example.pinyin: Lǎobǎn gěi wǒ yī ge xīn rènwù.
example.english: The boss gave me a new task.

gloss: to take (a photo); to pat; to clap
note: 拍照 pāi zhào (take photos), 拍手 pāi shǒu (clap), 拍電影 pāi diàn yǐng (shoot a film). MOE lists rare other readings (pā, bó, pò) not used in speech.

example.trad: 可以幫我們拍一張照嗎？
example.pinyin: Kěyǐ bāng wǒmen pāi yī zhāng zhào ma?
example.english: Could you take a picture of us?

example.pinyin: Zhēnde hěn gǎnxiè nǐ de bāngmáng.
example.english: Thank you so much for your help.

note: Listen for the tone: 賣 mài (4th, sell) vs 買 mǎi (3rd, buy). Taiwan says 有賣 yǒu mài for 'sells/has': 有賣咖啡嗎 yǒu mài kā fēi ma?

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn yǒu mài kāfēi ma?

gloss: related to; to have to do with
note: Pattern: A 跟 gēn B 有關 yǒu guān (A has to do with B). In casual speech 有關係 yǒu guān xì is common.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì gēn tā yǒuguān.
example.english: This has something to do with him.

note: 不舒服 bù shū fu means 'feeling unwell'. MOE gives a light second syllable; many Taiwanese say shū fú.
Also used between male friends (bro). MOE also has xiōng di, meaning younger brother. Siblings in general: 兄弟姊妹 xiōng dì jiě mèi (also written 兄弟姐妹 xiōng dì jiě mèi).

example.english: The two of them are brothers.

example.pinyin: Tiānqì huì yǐngxiǎng wǒ de xīnqíng.

note: Taiwan (MOE) says yán jiù; mainland says yán jiū.

example.english: He does research at a university.

example.trad: 這家飯店有提供早餐嗎？
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàndiàn yǒu tígōng zǎocān ma?

gloss: to point at; to mean; finger
note: 你是指 nǐ shì zhǐ… means 'do you mean…?'. As a noun it means finger, usually 手指 shǒu zhǐ.
Free of charge is 免費 miǎn fèi, not 自由 zì yóu.
Short form of 今天晚上 jīn tiān wǎn shang, which is just as common in speech.

example.pinyin: Jīnwǎn yào bù yào yīqǐ chīfàn?
example.english: Do you want to have dinner together tonight?
How are you going to prove it?
After work I go straight home.

note: 家 jiā is the everyday word for home/family; 家人 jiā rén means family members.

example.english: Let me think it over a bit more.

note: Letters are counted with 封 fēng. As a verb it is short for 相信 xiāng xìn: 我不信 wǒ bù xìn 'I don't believe it'. MOE also lists a literary reading shēn, not used in speech.

example.pinyin: Wǒ shōudào nǐ de xìn le.

note: 送 sòng sends things; 派 pài sends people on a task. Also a noun: faction, school of thought, and 'pie' (蘋果派 píng guǒ pài).

example.english: The company sent him to Japan.

note: Many uses: 生小孩 shēng xiǎo hái have a baby, 生病 shēng bìng get sick, 生氣 shēng qì get angry, 生的 shēng de raw/uncooked.

example.pinyin: Tā xià ge yuè yào shēng le.

note: Sounds like 死 sǐ 'death', so four is considered unlucky. Listen for the tone: 四 sì vs 十 shí (ten), which can sound alike in Taiwan accents.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā yǒu sì ge rén.
example.english: There are four people in our family.

note: Counts portions of food (一份早餐 yī fèn zǎo cān), copies of documents or newspapers, jobs (一份工作 yī fèn gōng zuò) and gifts (一份禮物 yī fèn lǐ wù). The archaic reading bīn is not used.

gloss: to laugh; to smile; to laugh at

note: Said when parting at night or going to bed, not as an evening greeting.

example.english: Good night, don't stay up too late!

note: Used for places: 市中心 shì zhōng xīn downtown, 購物中心 gòu wù zhōng xīn shopping mall. The plain middle of something is 中間 zhōng jiān.

example.pinyin: Táiběi shì yī ge dà chéngshì.

note: Often starts a sentence to draw a conclusion: 看來 kàn lái… 'it looks like…'. Similar to 好像 hǎo xiàng.

example.english: Looks like it's going to rain.

note: Taiwan keeps the full tone on 生 shēng (xué shēng); the mainland says xué sheng.
Counts dishes of food (一道菜 yī dào cài), questions (一道題 yī dào tí), doors and walls. Also 'road; way' in compounds like 道路 dào lù and 味道 wèi dào (flavor).

gloss: to choose; to pick; to elect
note: Everyday short form of 選擇 xuǎn zé. Also 'to elect': 選總統 xuǎn zǒng tǒng elect a president. 挑 tiāo is similar but means picking out carefully.

example.pinyin: Nǐ yào xuǎn nǎ yī ge?
example.english: Which one do you want to pick?

hint: a bit formal; not yě xǔ
note: Slightly more formal than 也許 yě xǔ and 可能 kě néng, which are more common in conversation.
Taiwan word; the mainland says 信息 xìn xī. Also means IT, as in 資訊業 zī xùn yè the IT industry. 資料 zī liào is data or materials (documents, files).

example.pinyin: Wǎnglù shàng yǒu hěn duō zīxùn.
example.english: There's a lot of information online.

note: Used in counting, phone numbers, floors and ordinals (第二 dì èr, 二十 èr shí). Before a measure word use 兩 liǎng instead: 兩個人 liǎng ge rén.

example.english: I live on the second floor.

hint: two syllables; turn into something else
note: Stresses a change from one state to another; 成為 chéng wéi is more formal.
A small doctor's office or clinic is 診所 zhěn suǒ.

example.english: I'm going to the hospital tomorrow.

note: Often 除了 chú le…以外 yǐ wài. With 都 dōu it excludes (除了我 chú le wǒ, 大家都去了 dà jiā dōu qù le everyone but me); with 也 yě/還 hái it adds (除了中文 chú le zhōng wén, 他還會日文 tā hái huì rì wén besides Chinese he also speaks Japanese).

example.pinyin: Chúle wǒ, dàjiā dōu qù le.
Zhìshǎo yào děng bàn ge xiǎoshí.
example.english: You have to wait at least half an hour.

note: More formal than 覺得 jué de; usually followed by a feeling, e.g. 感到很高興 gǎn dào hěn gāo xìng.
In speech, 塊 kuài is the word for dollars (一百塊 yī bǎi kuài = NT$100; 元 yuán is the written form). Also counts pieces and chunks: 一塊蛋糕 yī kuài dàn gāo a piece of cake.

example.english: A cup of coffee is fifty dollars.
